title: caucalis infesta subsp. purpurea
intro: Caucalis infesta subsp. purpurea, commonly known as Wild Carrot or Wild Queen Anne's Lace, is a plant species in the carrot family (Apiaceae) that is native to Europe and Western Asia. This plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its health benefits, which include reducing inflammation, soothing digestive issues, and acting as an expectorant to relieve respiratory problems. The therapeutic actions of Caucalis infesta subsp. purpurea include its anti-inflammatory, anti-spasmodic, and anti-cough properties, which have been attributed to its ability to relax muscles and thin mucus. The bioactive constituents of this plant include sesquiterpene lactones and essential oils, which contribute to its medicinal properties, although more research is needed to confirm its full range of bioactive compounds.
